subject: Performance Pact — pilot SLOs and action tracker
messages:
From: Alyssa Turner <alyssa.turner@healthgrid.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.example>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.example>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.example>
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: baseline targets & next steps

Thanks again for the demo today — the team found the streaming and KV-cache behavior promising. A couple of asks we have before we lock the pilot: 

- Confirm achievable p50/p95 latency for 2k token streaming (no chunking) at both single-tenant and reserved shared pools.
- Expected throughput: steady-state qps with 8 concurrent workers hitting different user sessions.
- Failure/fallback behavior if a node goes into degraded perf (what does Redwood fall back to?).

I've attached our baseline traffic sketch and a short list of API patterns we use. Can you put together the SLO items and a simple MAP for the pilot (owners + dates)? We need this to present to procurement next week.

Attachments: pilot_run_specs.pdf (pdf, 120KB)

Best,
Alyssa Turner
Director, Platform Engineering
HealthGrid

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.example>
To: Alyssa Turner <alyssa.turner@healthgrid.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.example>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.example>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: baseline targets & next steps

Hi Alyssa — great questions, thanks for the clear list. Summary and proposed commitments below; I attached an editable worksheet (SLO_worksheet_v1.xlsx) for you to comment on.

High-level proposed SLOs (pilot, 4 weeks):
- Latency (streaming, 2k tokens, no client-side chunking): p50 <= 350ms, p95 <= 1.2s for reserved single-tenant pool in us-west region.
- Concurrency/throughput: 8 concurrent sessions per model replica -> target steady qps ~22 requests/sec per replica (typical request = 1–2 streaming tokens/sec after prompt).
- Cold-start / degraded fallback: automatic routing to compatible smaller-quantized variant with graceful degrade to p95 <= 2.8s; alerts and automatic ticket creation if fallback occurs >0.5% of requests over 1h.
- Availability: 99.5% request-success over rolling 7d during pilot (excludes planned maintenance).

Open clarifications we need from HealthGrid (please confirm in-line in the sheet):
1) Typical prompt lengths and distribution (we saw your sketch, need percentiles).
2) Acceptable p95 window — some orgs prioritize p50 for UX; others need p95 for SLA.
3) Maximum acceptable fallbacks per hour before automated escalation.

Next steps / MAP (proposed):
- T-0 (today): Share worksheet (attached) — action: HealthGrid to annotate (Alyssa) — due Mon 26 Apr
- T+1: Redwood to run baseline pilot sim on reserved pool using HealthGrid traffic sketch (Marcus) — due Wed 28 Apr
- T+3: Execute 4-week pilot and collect telemetry (Monica) — pilot start Fri 30 Apr
- T+31: Pilot review and decision (contracting/procurement loop) — Tue 4 May

Attachments: SLO_worksheet_v1.xlsx (xlsx, 90KB)

Notes: We'll instrument token-level latency and stream chunk timing so we can separate model-side generation latency vs network buffering.

Thanks — Tessa

Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0193

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.example>
To: Alyssa Turner <alyssa.turner@healthgrid.com>, Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.example>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.example>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: baseline targets & next steps

Adding a few technical clarifications and a lightweight acceptance checklist for the pilot run.

Technical clarifications:
- Concurrency model: when you say 8 concurrent workers, do they maintain persistent SSE/websocket streams per session? If so we need to validate per-connection memory (KV cache) overhead — plan assumes ~400MB/session for the largest model.
- Encryption/keys: HealthGrid mentioned HSM-backed KMS in the demo — confirm if pilot needs HSM or software KMS only. HSM path adds ~60–80ms to cold-starts for model loading.

Pilot acceptance checklist (engineer-focused):
- End-to-end streaming test: 1k synthetic sessions over 30m window, measure p50/p95/tail.
- Graceful fallback test: induce a node degradation and confirm routing to compatible variant; fallback rate should be below 0.5% as agreed.
- Throughput soak: 8 concurrent workers for 2h at steady qps, no request failures >0.2% and CPU/GPU utilization within 70–85%.

Action owner assignments (short):
- HealthGrid annotate traffic percentiles: Alyssa (due 2027-04-26) — pending
- Redwood baseline run and report: Marcus (due 2027-04-28) — in progress
- Pilot instrumentation & run: Monica (due 2027-04-30)
- Pilot review & procurement packet: Tessa (due 2027-05-04)

I'll kick off the baseline sim script tomorrow morning once we have the annotated sketch.

Marcus Lin
Senior Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Alyssa Turner <alyssa.turner@healthgrid.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.example>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.example>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.example>, Samir Rao <samir.rao@healthgrid.com>, operations@healthgrid.com
Date: Tue, 27 Apr 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: baseline targets & next steps

Thanks — this is helpful and actionable. A few quick confirmations: 

- Sessions: yes, persistent websocket streams per user session. We'll add more detail in the worksheet by EOD today.
- HSM: procurement prefers software KMS for pilot (HSM in production only).
- Timeline: we can commit to annotating the sheet by today (27 Apr) and are comfortable with your proposed pilot start on 30 Apr.

Can Redwood also provide a short one-page summary we can share with procurement outlining the fallback behavior, monitoring triggers, and cost/availability tradeoffs? That would speed internal sign-off.

We'll also need an initial quote for the 4-week reserved pool to include in the procurement packet — can someone from commercial attach a ballpark? If you want, I can route a procurement contact into this thread.

Thanks,
Alyssa
